simple.meaning: כָּרַר (kârar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to dance (i.e. whirl).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in 2 Samuel, beginning at 2 Samuel 6:14. The surrounding contexts include family line, kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּרַר (H3769) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כָּרַר (kârar) / H3769 is traced through 2 Samuel 6:14, 2 Samuel 6:16 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: David danced before Yahweh with all his might; and David was clothed in a linen ephod.
As Yahweh’s ark came into David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out through the window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before Yahweh; and she despised him in her heart.
